provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

provenance.original: STP Development and Submission, Amendments, and Security Training Recordkeeping.  TSA is consolidating this collection with OMB control number 1652-0066 Security Training Program for Surface Transportation Employees.  Under 1652-0066, TSA required that owner/operators of certain freight railroads, PTPRs, and OTRB companies submit a security training program to TSA and maintain security training records. It takes approximately 8 hours to amend an STP, and TSA assumes this task is performed by a Security Coordinator.  TSA applies a fully loaded wage rate of $90.62 for the Security Coordinator. provenance.original: Aircraft Operators covered under this program must submit information for all passengers to Secure Flight in the form of SFPD.  The vast majority of SFPD messages submitted by the Aircraft Operators are identified as a low or neutral risk by the Secure Fight automated engine.  Those records identified as requiring additional review are inhibited by the Secure Flight engine, and the passengers with inhibited boarding pass must go the Aircraft Operator ticket counter for additional assistance.  Aircraft Operators must submit additional information on inhibited passengers to TSA.  Generally, this information is gathered from the passenger’s VID and submitted electronically to TSA (a VID submission).  There are currently 222 Aircraft Operators covered by this collection; in addition, TSA expects 20 Aircraft Operators per year to be added each year.  TSA estimates an average of 990 annual VID submissions per covered Aircraft Operator, and 130 seconds (0.0361 hours) per response.  Certain submissions may require a Resolution Call to TSA to provide additional information.  TSA estimates that each carrier will be required to make an average of 230 calls per year.  TSA estimates a Resolution Call will require 12 minutes (0.2 hours).  The total annual hour burden for covered Aircraft Operators is 21,418.5 hours, or 64,256 hours over 3 years.  Table 1 summarizes these estimates.
